title: Behaviour-shaping of pathways could be an alternative to gene therapy

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Behaviour-shaping of pathways could be an alternative to gene therapy

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Rational stimulation regimes derived from computational models of pathway memory could control pathway function without genomic editing or network rewiring, so behaviour-shaping of pathway responses stands as a potential biomedical alternative to gene therapy (e.g. to counter drug pharmacoresistance and sensitization).

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Rational control of dynamic pathway function using stimuli derived from computational models opens the door to empirical studies of proto-cognitive capacities in unconventional embodiments and suggests numerous possible applications in biomedicine, where behavior shaping of pathway responses stand as a potential alternative to gene therapy.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “Abstract”. Scope: Gene regulatory and protein pathways in cells and tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-03: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.43

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed alternative has measurable outcomes, but simulations alone cannot establish biomedical substitutability. Existing models can nominate regimens, while decisive tests require new perturbation and therapeutic-response data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For matched disease-relevant pathways, compare model-derived stimulation regimens with gene-editing interventions on restoration of function, durability, toxicity, and resistance. The claim is supported only if stimulation controls function comparably without genomic alteration.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public models do not establish therapeutic efficacy in cells or patients.

A fair comparison with gene therapy requires new matched intervention data.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.2
data existence: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The models and code can show that stimulation changes a simulated response without rewiring, which is only a proxy for the biomedical claim. Nothing public tests whether that strategy substitutes for gene therapy against pharmacoresistance or sensitization in cells or patients. The claim as a therapeutic proposal stays only partly testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the published pathway ODEs, test whether a stimulation schedule found by the memory search changes a designated response without editing parameters or edges, and compare that in silico control with the absence of any public study in which such a schedule replaces a gene-therapy outcome. In-model control without rewiring would support only the computational half; a therapeutic alternative would require a failed or successful head-to-head that does not yet exist.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A hedged 'potential alternative' is compatible with both success and failure of future trials.

No public dataset compares behaviour-shaping of a pathway with genomic editing on a clinical or cellular endpoint.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.4

operationalizability: 0.42
data adequacy: 0.3
